source.prompt: (the American robin's) An American robin (Turdus migratorius), one adult male standing on the ground, side-on pose, upright alert thrush posture, wings folded tight against the body. Realistic proportions: 25 cm long, a round chest, a medium-long tail, a straight yellow bill, long thin legs. Dark grey-brown back, wings and tail, a blackish head with a broken white eye ring, a white-streaked throat, a brick-red orange breast and belly, white under the tail. Three toes forward and one back. No base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: A variant of the American robin's Meshy preview (no credits), scaled to 0.24 m, pitched 10 degrees nose-down (more level than the robin), a shorter 8.5 cm square tail. Colours (the male): slate blue-grey back, crown, wings and tail; an orange eyebrow over a black mask through the eye and cheek; orange throat and upper breast, a black breast band, orange lower breast and flanks (the flanks washed slate), grey-white belly scalloped grey on lod0, white undertail; two orange wing bars and an orange stripe on the folded wing (lod0 and lod1); orange bars on the flight cards and a buff-orange underwing stripe; dark bill, pinkish-brown legs. Triangles: lod0 1,000 = 815 body + 185 legs, tail, cards, eyes; lod1 400 = 311 body + 89 legs, tail, cards, eyes; lod2 120 = 93 body + 27 legs, tail, cards, eyes. GLB 172,432 bytes. lod_m is a suggestion.

rig: bird rig template of the Steller's jay (tools/build_stellersjay.py; drawn with client/src/animalModels.js RIG.stjay's constants): PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 / LEG_B 2 procedural legs (pivot at the knee), TAIL 3 procedural tail (pivot at the rump), HEAD 6 (head and neck, pivot at the base of the neck), WING_L/R 4/5 and HAND_L/R 9/10 flight cards that collapse into the shoulder on pose; extras.rig {kind 'bird', wing (shoulder), tail (rump), head (neck base), length_m}; no skin
accuracy_notes: Built 2026-11-05. Reads as a varied thrush: slate and orange, the black breast band and mask, the orange eyebrow. Still open: the folded wing's bars and stripe are only a few faces wide and break up; the robin's body is a little slim for this chunkier thrush; male only (no _COLORB for the browner female).
